title: Epsilon–delta implication
parts: If x is within δ of a but different from a,
then f(x) is within ε of L.
example: For f(x) = 2x, a = 1 and L = 2, choose δ = ε/2 to make the implication hold.
note: In a limit proof, a suitable δ is chosen for every ε > 0.
wrong: The difference between x and a must exceed δ.
δ is chosen once and works for every function.

title: Supremum
parts: sup S
The least upper bound of S.
example: sup(0,1) = 1 even though 1 is not in the interval.
note: The supremum is a maximum only when it belongs to the set.
wrong: The greatest member of S, which must always exist.
The greatest lower bound of S.

title: Infimum
parts: inf S
The greatest lower bound of S.
note: Every element of S is at least its infimum when it exists.
wrong: The least upper bound of S.
The smallest member, which always belongs to S.

title: Sequence convergence
parts: aₙ → L
The terms aₙ approach L as n tends to infinity.
example: 1/n → 0 as n grows, although no term is zero.
note: Converging to L does not require reaching L.
wrong: The series of all terms always sums to L.

title: Cauchy condition
parts: d(xₙ,xₘ) < ε
The distance between sufficiently late terms can be made smaller than any ε > 0.
example: For xₙ = 1/n, take n,m > 2/ε to ensure |1/n − 1/m| < ε.
note: The condition compares two terms. It does not name a limiting point.
wrong: Every term must be within ε of x₁.
The sequence is constant from some index onwards.

title: Complex conjugate
parts: z̄ = a − bi
The conjugate of z = a + bi reverses the imaginary part.
note: Conjugation leaves the real part alone.
wrong: Change only the sign of the real part.

title: Modulus of a complex number
parts: |z| = √(a² + b²)
The distance of z = a + bi from the origin.
note: The modulus is a non-negative real number.
wrong: The magnitude of the imaginary part alone.

title: Argument of a complex number
parts: arg(z)
An angle from the positive real axis to the nonzero complex number z.
example: For z = i, an argument is π/2.
note: Arguments can differ by multiples of 2π. A principal argument chooses a standard range.
wrong: The distance from z to the origin.

title: Contour integral
parts: ∮γ
Integrate along the closed curve γ
f(z) dz
the complex function f with respect to z.
example: ∮γ 1/z dz = 2πi on the positively oriented unit circle.
note: Orientation matters. Reversing the path reverses the sign.
wrong: Integrate the real part only between two real endpoints.
Find the length of γ regardless of f.
